ethiopia.content: Kenya raises flag over insecurity in Ethiopia, Somalia - The EastAfrican Today's Paper | Our Brands Home East Africa Southern Africa Central Africa West Africa North Africa World Africa Eastern Africa More ••• Sign in My Account Personal details Change password Purchases Sign out Search Home News East Africa Southern Africa Central Africa West Africa North Africa World Africa Eastern Africa Business & Tech Opinion Columnists Editorials Cartoon Guest Blogs Sustainability Innovation Health Climate Magazine Services Today's Paper Our Brands Prime Kenya raises flag over insecurity in Ethiopia, Somalia Friday, November 27, 2026 - 5 min read Ethiopians sit at a holding ground after fights erupted in the Ethiopian border town of Moyale, Kenya on October 23, 2026. Photo credit: Reuters By SAMWEL OWINO Thank you for reading businessdailyafrica.com Show plans Kenya has expressed concern that political instability and insecurity, coupled with increased activities of extremist groups in the Horn, risk spilling into the country and affecting its national interests. President William Ruto noted in the State of National Security report tabled in Parliament this week that growing terrorist groups in countries such as Somalia, armed conflict in Ethiopia and the forthcoming general election in South Sudan in December could have a spillover effect on Kenya. The State of National Security report covers the period from September 2025 to August 31, 2026 and outlines the prevailing and emerging threats to national security and the Government’s strategic responses. Related Eastern Africa PRIME Ethiopia is rising, but conflicts threaten the gains Nov 07 - 6 min read Eastern Africa What is driving renewed fighting in Ethiopia? Oct 01 - 8 min read “Kenya continues to face a persistent and adaptive terrorism and violent extremism threat, mainly linked to Al-Shabaab, with heightened risk along the Kenya–Somalia border counties of Mandera, Garissa, Wajir and Lamu, as well as major urban centres including Nairobi and Mombasa,” reads the report. Read: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears, sources say Through the report, President Ruto noted that Kenya’s proximity to the al-Shabaab operating environment in Somalia, particularly areas bordering North Eastern and Coastal Kenya, continues to present a direct security concern through cross-border infiltration, recruitment, facilitation and the movement of terrorist operatives and materiel. Terrorism “While the terrorism threat remains particularly pronounced along the Kenya– Somalia border and parts of the Coast, vulnerabilities to radicalisation and violent extremism extend beyond the traditional high-risk areas,” reads the report. Ethiopian families displaced by violence in Moyale. Photo credit: Reuters According to the report, Eastern Africa remains one of Africa’s most active terrorism theatres, with instability in Somalia continuing to have spill-over effects on Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda. “Al-Shabaab remains the principal terrorist threat within the region and continues to exploit instability in Somalia to sustain its operations and extend its activities across the region,” reads the report. According to the report, the group retains the capability to conduct Improvised Explosive Device (IED) attacks, ambushes, assassinations, cross-border incursions and attacks on security and civilian infrastructure, supported by decentralised cells, online radicalisation, extremist propaganda, criminal networks and socio-economic grievances. President Ruto noted that emerging radicalisation and violent extremism concerns have also been reported in Kenya's Nakuru, Nyeri, Siaya, Kisumu, Kakamega and Migori Counties, driven by youth unemployment, political and intercommunal tensions, land disputes, religious manipulation and digital influence platforms. During the reporting period, 37 terror-related incidents were reported, including 21 active shooter incidents, 14 IED attacks, one kidnapping incident and one foiled terror attempt. Comparatively, the previous period recorded [figure to be inserted]. “The al-Shabaab group sustained probing attacks against security establishments, telecommunication masts, power infrastructure, IED ambushes and asymmetric attacks on security vehicles along Main Supply Routes, particularly in Fafi and Lamu East Sub-Counties of Garissa and Lamu Counties,” reads the report. The report noted that the terror group continues to thrive in the region by exploiting border vulnerabilities and regional instability to sustain its operational presence and activities. President Ruto said the government has sustained intelligence-led and multi-agency counter-terrorism operations, including enhanced collection, analysis and timely sharing of intelligence among relevant security agencies to identify and disrupt terrorist activities and networks in order to combat the terror threats. In addition, President Ruto said the government has also enhanced border security through sustained patrols along the Kenya-Somalia border and coordinated operations with regional partners. However, despite the efforts, President Ruto noted that porous borders, which facilitate militant infiltration, the movement of weapons and illicit financial flows, continue to jeopardise government efforts to contain the activities of the group. He also pointed out that the group has continued to exploit the socio-economic vulnerabilities and perceived marginalisation of some regions to recruit its members. In the Horn of Africa, the report notes that the heightened political contestation in Somalia, over the planned transition from the clan-based election model to universal suffrage, might have security implications in Kenya. “The prevailing conditions are compounding the risk of structural volatility, with adverse implications on Kenya’s national interests,” reads the report. In Ethiopia, the report noted that the contestation of the outcome of the recent general election has significant implications for the Horn of Africa, including potential refugee flows, cross-border arms trafficking, and increased tensions with neighbouring states over resource issues. This report does not cover recent events such as the clashes at the Moyale border between the two countries, where at least 40,000 people crossed into Kenya in October to escape clashes between two communities that have contested land ownership for decades. Read: African insurgents take war to the skies with off-the-shelf drones For South Sudan, President Ruto pointed out that the general election in December this year could lead to heightened political contestation due to differences between the Transitional National Government of South Sudan and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement in Opposition. “This, coming in the backdrop of persistent conflicts in parts of the country, could have a spill-over effect on Kenya,” reads the report. Globally, President Ruto noted that the US-Israel-Iran war disrupted fuel supply and affected cargo flights, leading to reduced exports to the international market. “The war in the Middle East also affected Kenyan diaspora remittances, food security, and Kenya’s general national security,” reads the report. On the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, President Ruto noted that the war continued to impact Kenya through covert recruitment of Kenyan nationals to fight in the war and economic shocks. “The protracted conflict also continued to exert pressure on Kenya to navigate the delicate balance between maintaining diplomatic relations and international partnerships, while ensuring sustained international market access,” reads the report. On a positive note, the President noted that Kenya and the European Union (EU) had unlocked duty-free, quota-free access to European markets, following the launch of the 10-year Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation Strategy in June 2026. ethiopia.summary: Kenya has raised alarms regarding the escalating insecurity in neighboring Ethiopia and Somalia, which poses a potential threat to its national interests. President William Ruto highlighted these concerns in the State of National Security report presented to Parliament, noting the risks associated with political instability, extremist activities, and the upcoming elections in South Sudan. The report, covering September 2025 to August 2026, indicates that Kenya faces persistent threats from terrorist groups, particularly Al-Shabaab, which exploits regional instability to conduct operations. Vulnerabilities to radicalization are spreading beyond traditional hotspots, driven by factors such as youth unemployment and political tensions. The report documented 37 terror-related incidents during the period, emphasizing the need for enhanced border security and intelligence-sharing among security agencies. Despite ongoing counter-terrorism efforts, porous borders and socio-economic grievances continue to facilitate militant activities. The report also warns of potential refugee flows and increased tensions due to electoral disputes in Ethiopia and South Sudan.

ethiopia.title: Eritrea Accuses Ethiopia of Using Maritime Diplomacy to 'Camouflage Its Irredentist Ambitions' - allAfrica.com
ethiopia.content: Eritrea Accuses Ethiopia of Using Maritime Diplomacy to 'Camouflage Its Irredentist Ambitions' - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Eritrea Accuses Ethiopia of Using Maritime Diplomacy to 'Camouflage Its Irredentist Ambitions' Pixabay, Pixabay Drapeau de l'Ethiopie et de l'Erythrée 27 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Eritrea has accused Ethiopia of using maritime diplomacy and regional security forums to mask what it described as territorial ambitions in the Horn of Africa, escalating tensions amid renewed disagreements over Ethiopia's pursuit of Red Sea access. In a statement issued Thursday, Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Prosperity Party government of seeking to "manufacture a veneer of international legitimacy" around its demand for "sovereign sea access," which Asmara characterized as territorial revisionism. The statement follows Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's address to the House of Peoples' Representatives on Thursday, November 26, in which he rejected claims that Ethiopia intends to invade Eritrea , but reiterated that access to the Red Sea remains a strategic imperative to be pursued through dialogue. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "Now they say, 'Ethiopia is going to invade Eritrea, Ethiopia will wage an invasion for the Red Sea'--we will not wage an invasion. Invasion is not needed; we want it peacefully and through dialogue," Abiy told lawmakers, likening Ethiopia's maritime ambitions to the natural course of the Abay River. Abiy claimed Ethiopia had made repeated efforts to pursue economic cooperation with Eritrea, including proposals to extend electricity infrastructure, build roads and jointly develop a port, but said the Eritrean government had rejected them. "We have made high efforts with the Eritrean government to develop together," he said, citing a proposal to supply electricity at Ethiopian domestic prices and jointly undertake infrastructure projects. He also said Ethiopia had undergone a "strategic awakening" after its political elite failed to properly recognize the country's Red Sea interests, arguing that neighboring countries should recognize the long-term strategic implications of the issue. Abiy further warned that Ethiopia's size and population meant instability within the country would have far-reaching regional consequences, cautioning against scenarios involving millions of Ethiopians moving into neighboring states. "Because we are a large population; our disturbance disturbs many," he said, arguing that Ethiopia's stability was central to wider regional peace. He also pointed to shifting geopolitical dynamics, including the potential opening of Arctic shipping routes, arguing that these could alter the Red Sea's strategic importance in the coming years. Eritrea, however, said Ethiopia's maritime diplomacy was increasingly being used to normalize the involvement of a landlocked country in Red Sea security arrangements. It cited a late-October maritime security and search-and-rescue workshop in Addis Abeba , supported by the European Union. The workshop brought together naval representatives from Puntland and Somaliland alongside representatives from Djibouti. Asmara argued that including Somali regional administrations while bypassing the Federal Government of Somalia undermined the sovereignty of a recognized coastal state. Eritrea also cited the Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa, held in Bahir Dar from October 23-25, where National Intelligence and Security Service Director General Redwan Hussein argued that Ethiopia should have a role in Red Sea security arrangements given the waterway's strategic importance and growing involvement of global powers. Redwan maintained that Red Sea security was not a responsibility reserved exclusively for coastal states, a position Eritrea said reflected Addis Abeba's efforts to expand its role in regional maritime affairs. The Eritrean statement further cited Field Marshal Birhanu Jula's November 13 remarks in Mekele, in which he reportedly asserted that Dogali, Gundet and Adulis belonged to Tigray and made claims concerning Somalia's port of Zeila. Asmara described the remarks as part of a broader territorial narrative advanced by Ethiopian political and military officials. It warned that repeated territorial assertions by senior officials, alongside threats to secure maritime access through force, challenged regional sovereignty and internationally recognized borders. The statement invoked Article 2(4) of the UN Charter, which prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of states. ethiopia.title: COP32 Offers Ethiopia a Strategic Path to Green Growth and Global Influence
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: COP32 Offers Ethiopia a Strategic Path to Green Growth and Global Influence - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: COP32 Offers Ethiopia a Strategic Path to Green Growth and Global Influence 27 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) When world leaders, policymakers, climate negotiators, investors, and development partners gather in Addis Ababa from November 8 to 19, 2027, for the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32), Ethiopia will take center stage in global climate diplomacy at a defining moment for the country and the African continent. Hosting the summit presents Ethiopia with a historic opportunity to strengthen its international standing, mobilize climate finance, attract green investment, deepen development partnerships, and accelerate its transition toward a climate-resilient, low-carbon economy. Beyond convening one of the world's largest diplomatic gatherings, COP32 provides Ethiopia with a powerful platform to place Africa's climate priorities at the heart of global negotiations while showcasing its progress in renewable energy, environmental restoration, sustainable transport, and green development. The opportunity also carries significant political and economic weight. For Ethiopia, COP32 is not simply an international conference to be organized and successfully delivered. It is an opportunity to translate diplomatic leadership into concrete development gains, positioning the country as a destination for climate investment and a prominent voice in shaping the future of global climate cooperation. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Ethiopia secured the hosting role following unanimous endorsement by the African Group of Negotiators at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, in November 2025, after Nigeria withdrew its competing bid in support of a unified African candidacy. The endorsement reflected continental confidence in Ethiopia's diplomatic standing and its growing engagement in international climate affairs. The conference also builds on Ethiopia's experience hosting the Second Africa Climate Summit in September 2025, which attracted more than 25,000 participants and produced the Addis Ababa Declaration. As the headquarters of the African Union, Addis Ababa is uniquely positioned to bring together world leaders, policymakers, development partners, climate experts, and investors. The Strategic Value of COP32 The strategic value of COP32 extends far beyond international recognition. It offers Ethiopia an opportunity to mobilize financing for renewable energy, climate-smart agriculture, resilient infrastructure, forest restoration, clean technologies, and sustainable urban development. It also provides a critical platform for advocating accessible, predictable, affordable, and concessional climate finance for African countries, which have contributed relatively little to historical global emissions but face disproportionately severe climate impacts. At COP29 in Baku, countries agreed on a new climate finance goal calling on developed countries to take the lead in mobilizing at least 300 billion USD annually for developing nations by 2035, within a broader ambition to scale climate finance from all sources to 1.3 trillion USD annually. Ethiopia can use its COP32 presidency to advocate for practical mechanisms that translate these commitments into accessible financing for vulnerable economies. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has consistently emphasized that climate action must be viewed as an economic and development priority rather than a narrowly environmental concern. Addressing the opening of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in November 2026, he stated: "In Ethiopia, climate action is economic policy." The statement captures an important dimension of Ethiopia's approach to climate change: environmental protection, economic transformation, agricultural productivity, energy development, and livelihood security are interconnected priorities. During the same conference, the Prime Minister called for climate financing that reaches vulnerable communities before disasters occur, stressing: "Funding should be agreed in advance. It can then move at the speed of our forecasters, while there is still time to save lives." These remarks offer a clear indication of the priorities Ethiopia intends to advance as it prepares to assume a prominent role in international climate diplomacy through COP32. Prime Minister Abiy has also highlighted the broader national benefits of hosting the conference. In convening the COP32 National Steering Committee on November 16, 2026, he described the summit as an opportunity to advance Ethiopia's climate and environmental agenda, strengthen international partnerships, attract investment, and translate national initiatives into lasting development outcomes. He further emphasized the need for a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to ensure that preparations are aligned and the country is ready to deliver a successful international conference. Domestic Transformation: Building Credibility Through Action Ethiopia's ambition to host COP32 is anchored in domestic initiatives demonstrating its commitment to environmental protection, renewable energy, and climate-resilient development. One of the most visible is the Green Legacy Initiative, launched in 2019. The nationwide program has mobilized millions of citizens in large-scale tree-planting and environmental restoration campaigns. Government figures indicate that more than 56 billion seedlings have been planted through the initiative, reflecting the scale of the country's efforts to restore degraded landscapes and expand green spaces. The initiative has become an important component of Ethiopia's environmental diplomacy. It also demonstrates how public participation can support national environmental objectives while creating awareness about the importance of protecting natural resources. Speaking at the Second Africa Climate Summit in Addis Ababa in September 2025, Prime Minister Abiy highlighted the initiative as an example of Ethiopia's homegrown climate solutions. He also articulated a broader African ambition, declaring: "We are not here to negotiate our survival. We are here to design the world's next climate economy." The statement reflects Ethiopia's intention to move beyond the conventional portrayal of Africa as merely a victim of climate change and instead position the continent as an active contributor to global climate solutions. In the energy sector, Ethiopia has steadily expanded its renewable electricity generation capacity through investments in hydropower, wind, and solar energy. The inauguration of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) in September 2025 marked a major milestone in the country's ambition to strengthen clean energy generation, expand electricity access, and increase regional power exports. Ethiopia has also taken significant steps toward sustainable transport. Since January 2024, the country has restricted imports of conventional petrol- and diesel-powered vehicles as part of its transition toward electric mobility. Although expanding charging infrastructure, ensuring vehicle affordability, and strengthening electricity distribution remain important priorities, the policy positions Ethiopia as an early mover in Africa's clean transport transition. These initiatives complement Ethiopia's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0), which targets a reduction in projected greenhouse gas emissions of up to 70.3 percent below business-as-usual levels by 2035, contingent on international support, alongside a long-term ambition of achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. However, Ethiopia's climate agenda extends beyond emissions reduction. Climate change poses significant risks to agriculture, food security, water resources, and rural livelihoods. World Bank assessments have estimated that climate impacts could cost the country between 1 and 1.5 percent of GDP annually, with the potential for substantially greater losses in the coming decades. Consequently, adaptation financing, climate-resilient agriculture, water resource management, early-warning systems, and disaster preparedness must remain central priorities in Ethiopia's preparations for COP32. This is particularly important given the Prime Minister's recent emphasis on early action and financial support for vulnerable communities. At COP31, he underscored the urgency of ensuring that climate finance is available when early warnings are issued and reaches those most exposed to climate risks. His appeal was particularly powerful when he observed: "Our farmers once trusted the seasons to arrive on time. Let us make sure our support does." The statement captures the human dimension of climate change and reinforces the importance of ensuring that international climate commitments produce tangible benefits for communities whose livelihoods depend on increasingly unpredictable weather patterns. Advancing Africa's Climate Priorities COP32 will give Ethiopia an influential platform to amplify Africa's collective position in international climate negotiations, particularly on climate finance, technology transfer, adaptation, and loss and damage. For African countries, the central challenge is balancing the urgent need for industrialization, energy access, employment creation, and agricultural modernization with the growing threats posed by climate change. Ethiopia can use its COP32 presidency to champion a development framework that recognizes Africa's right to economic transformation while supporting clean energy, environmental protection, and climate resilience. At the Second Africa Climate Summit, Prime Minister Abiy offered a particularly important perspective on the continent's position in the global climate economy. He called for a shift in how international partners approach Africa's climate ambitions, stating: "It is time to replace climate aid with climate investment. This is not charity. It is the most strategic investment humanity can make." This position could become a defining theme of Ethiopia's COP32 diplomacy. Rather than treating Africa primarily as a recipient of climate assistance, Ethiopia can advocate for investment partnerships that recognize the continent's enormous renewable energy potential, agricultural resources, biodiversity, critical minerals, and young population. The continent has considerable opportunities to develop solar, wind, geothermal, and hydropower resources, expand green industrialization, strengthen sustainable agriculture, and build climate-resilient infrastructure. However, realizing these opportunities requires affordable financing, technology transfer, capacity building, and stronger international partnerships. COP32 should therefore provide a platform for moving beyond declarations toward practical investment agreements, bankable projects, and measurable implementation commitments. The summit will also offer Ethiopia an opportunity to showcase its tourism potential, biodiversity, cultural heritage, and emerging economic opportunities. From the historical landmarks of Aksum and Lalibela to the Simien and Bale Mountains, the Great Rift Valley, and Lake Tana, Ethiopia possesses considerable natural and cultural assets that can reinforce its broader green growth narrative. Hosting thousands of international delegates will also generate economic opportunities across tourism, hospitality, transport, construction, and other service industries. Investments in conference facilities, urban infrastructure, transport networks, accommodation, and digital connectivity could produce economic benefits extending well beyond the summit. Turning COP32 into Lasting National Gains With less than a year remaining before the summit opens, effective implementation will be decisive in turning Ethiopia's hosting responsibilities into lasting national benefits. The government's establishment of coordination structures and engagement with international partners, alongside Prime Minister Abiy's convening of the National Steering Committee, signals the importance attached to a coordinated national preparation process. Successful delivery will require targeted investments in conference venues, hospitality, public transport, security, telecommunications, and urban environmental management. Equally important will be the participation of the private sector, universities, research institutions, civil society organizations, youth groups, and local communities. The private sector, in particular, has an important role to play in converting the international attention generated by COP32 into investment opportunities. Businesses operating in renewable energy, electric mobility, construction, agriculture, tourism, manufacturing, and financial services should be encouraged to develop partnerships and investment proposals ahead of the conference. Ethiopia must also ensure that its domestic climate achievements are supported by transparent implementation and measurable results. Expanding last-mile electricity access, scaling up clean cooking solutions, strengthening electric vehicle infrastructure, improving climate-smart agricultural practices, and monitoring the long-term survival of planted trees are among the important benchmarks that can demonstrate progress. The conference should also provide an opportunity to strengthen Ethiopia's institutional capacity for climate finance mobilization, project preparation, environmental governance, and international partnership management. Ultimately, the country's credibility as a climate host will depend not only on its ability to organize a successful international gathering but also on its capacity to demonstrate that its climate ambitions are translating into practical development outcomes. A Defining Opportunity for Ethiopia and Africa COP32 represents both an international responsibility and a defining national opportunity for Ethiopia. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's vision of moving from climate aid toward climate investment, combined with his emphasis on early action, accessible financing, and climate-resilient development, provides an important foundation for shaping Ethiopia's engagement with the international community. The country's presidency can help advance a more balanced global climate agenda--one that recognizes Africa's development aspirations, acknowledges its disproportionate vulnerability to climate impacts, and creates opportunities for the continent to participate more meaningfully in the emerging global green economy. For Ethiopia, the challenge is to ensure that the diplomatic visibility and international partnerships generated by COP32 translate into renewable energy investments, stronger infrastructure, employment opportunities, improved livelihoods, and greater climate resilience. The ultimate measure of Ethiopia's COP32 presidency will not simply be the successful organization of a global summit in Addis Ababa. It will be the extent to which the conference helps convert international commitments into tangible investments, strengthens Africa's voice in global climate governance, and delivers lasting benefits for Ethiopians and the wider African continent. ethiopia.title: Uganda and Ethiopia Deepen Cooperation On Strategic Diaspora Mobilisation, Investment, and Knowledge Transfer
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Uganda and Ethiopia Deepen Cooperation On Strategic Diaspora Mobilisation, Investment, and Knowledge Transfer - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Uganda and Ethiopia Deepen Cooperation On Strategic Diaspora Mobilisation, Investment, and Knowledge Transfer 27 November 2026 The Independent (Kampala) Addis Ababa — Ahead of the 3 rd Annual Uganda Diaspora Convention 2026, a high- level Ugandan Inter-Ministerial Presidential Benchmarking Delegation, led by the Minister of State for Finance, Planning and Economic Development (Planning), Hon. Amos Lugoloobi, held bilateral consultations yesterday, 25 November 2026, with Ambassador Lencho Bati, Director-General of the Ethiopian Diaspora Service (EDS). The engagement forms a central pillar of Uganda's five-day benchmarking mission to the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (23-27 November 2026), aimed at adapting proven legal, institutional, financial, and digital mechanisms to operationalise Uganda's first comprehensive National Diaspora Support and Engagement Policy. Uganda's Vision: Moving Beyond Remittances to Investment and Technology Transfer Addressing the meeting, Hon. Amos Lugoloobi noted that His Excellency President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni specifically tasked the delegation with visiting Addis Ababa to study Ethiopia's transformation and pioneering diaspora engagement frameworks. Hon. Lugoloobi highlighted the shared history between the two nations and acknowledged the vital role remittances play in stabilizing Uganda's currency and supporting debt servicing, with inflows having more than doubled from approximately USD 1.4 billion in 2024 to USD 3.03 billion in FY 2025/26. "Uganda has a large diaspora, particularly in the United Kingdom, whose remittances already play a crucial role in supporting our economy," said Hon. Amos Lugoloobi. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "However, we now wish to move beyond just remittances. We are here to learn from Ethiopia's remarkable success in leveraging its diaspora for flagship national projects like the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, and to adopt institutional arrangements for mapping diaspora skills, driving technology transfer, and expanding productive investment." The Ugandan delegation, comprising senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development (MoFPED), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), Office of the Solicitor General, State House, Bank of Uganda (BoU), Capital Markets Authority (CMA), National Planning Authority (NPA), and Ministry of Internal Affairs, sought detailed insights into diaspora registration systems, investor safeguards, and capital-market instruments. Ethiopia's Experience: National Cohesion, Flagship Projects, and Origin Identification Welcoming the Ugandan delegation, Ambassador Lencho Bati underscored the importance of shifting the global narrative around African immigrants from negative stereotypes to recognizing their massive contributions as cultural, financial, and tourism ambassadors. Ambassador Bati shared how integrating the diaspora into national reconciliation efforts and Vision 2050 has fostered healing, unity, and substantial capital inflows. "Diaspora engagement is a powerful catalyst for national cohesion and economic transformation, especially when communities are united around flagship national projects like the Renaissance Dam," stated Ambassador Lencho Bati, Director-General of the Ethiopian Diaspora Service. "By understanding the professional backgrounds of our diaspora, engaging second-generation youth through their cultural roots, and offering practical incentives like origin-identification cards to ease investment fears, nations can unlock immense developmental potential." Ambassador Bati also emphasized the value of proactive international outreach to listen to diaspora grievances, alongside utilizing structured diaspora associations for targeted engagement. Next Steps for the Benchmarking Mission Insights gathered from the Addis Ababa consultations will directly inform proposed legislative principles, targeted financial products, and an inter-ministerial action matrix to be submitted to the Right Honourable Prime Minister and Cabinet. Following the Ethiopia leg, the delegation will conduct a parallel benchmarking mission to New Delhi, India, from 7 to 11 December 2026. Consolidated findings and proposals from both countries will be unveiled and tested during Uganda's Annual Diaspora Convention scheduled for 18-22 December 2026 at Speke Resort Munyonyo. somalia.content: Somalia to begin issuing East African Community e-passports in January 2027 - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Somalia to begin issuing East African Community e-passports in January 2027 Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Friday November 27, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — Somalia will begin issuing East African Community (EAC) electronic passports in January 2027 after completing production of the new travel document, marking another step toward integrating its immigration system with those of other East African countries, the regional bloc announced Friday. The announcement followed a meeting of EAC immigration chiefs in Kampala, Uganda, on Thursday, Nov. 26, where Somali officials presented the country's new third-generation electronic passport and confirmed that preparations for its rollout had been finalized. advertisements In a statement issued Nov. 27, the EAC said the passport would be linked to Somalia's national identification system, while issuance services were also expected to be available through Somali diplomatic missions abroad. The new document is intended to improve travel security, facilitate regional mobility and support Somalia's implementation of the EAC Common Market Protocol, which promotes the free movement of people, workers and services. Somalia's Immigration and Citizenship Agency Director General Hussein Qasim Yusuf, who led the country's delegation to the Kampala meeting, said the rollout reflected efforts to modernize immigration services and align national identification systems with regional standards. "Somalia, as the newest Partner State, is honoured to sit fully at this table. We come to this meeting conscious that immigration is at the heart of integration," Yusuf said. He said Somalia was developing a unified identity verification system linking civil registration, national identification cards, electronic passports and border management systems. "Somalia is building one verifiable identity chain from civil registration, to National ID, which is now mandatory for passports, to the ICAO-compliant e-Passport with the EAC insignia, and ultimately to our border systems," Yusuf said. The new passports will incorporate modern security features that meet International Civil Aviation Organization standards while carrying the EAC insignia and elements reflecting Somalia's national identity. According to the EAC, the regional passport system is intended to make cross-border travel more secure and efficient while supporting trade, employment and other economic opportunities. EAC Deputy Secretary General Andrea Ariik Malueth welcomed Somalia's progress, describing the planned issuance as an important step toward implementing regional integration commitments. "Beyond the document itself, this is about bringing our citizens closer together, facilitating movement for trade, employment and other opportunities," Malueth said. The announcement follows Somalia's earlier approval to adopt the EAC passport design. In December 2025, Somalia received authorization to use the regional passport format, allowing the government to proceed with preparations for production and issuance. The authorization was formally handed over to Somalia's Minister of Internal Security, Abdullahi Sheikh Ismail Fartaag, in February 2026 by Somalia's ambassador to Tanzania and permanent representative to the EAC, Ilyas Ali Hassan. The EAC electronic passport was introduced in March 2016 and is issued in three categories: ordinary, service and diplomatic. Five member states, Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and Tanzania, already issue EAC electronic passports, while South Sudan has reported progress toward introducing the document. Somalia formally joined the EAC on March 4, 2024, becoming the bloc's eighth member state. Since joining, the federal government has been working to align its immigration, trade and identification systems with regional requirements. During the Kampala meeting, immigration chiefs also discussed the use of electronic national identity cards as travel documents, visa-free entry arrangements and efforts to harmonize entry, work and residence permit procedures and fees. Officials emphasized the need to reduce barriers to movement while strengthening border security and cooperation among member states. The EAC said Somalia's planned passport rollout would help advance those objectives and strengthen the country's participation in the regional community. Somalia's third-generation passport was unveiled at a meeting of East Africa's meeting immigration chiefs. / Others Somalia has presented its new third-generation electronic passport to East African Community (EAC) member states, marking another step towards regional integration and the modernisation of its immigration system. The passport was showcased during a three-day meeting of immigration chiefs in Kampala, Uganda, which concluded on Thursday. Somalia’s delegation was led by Hussein Qasim Yusuf, Director-General of the Immigration and Citizenship Agency, who briefed regional officials on the passport’s advanced security features and technology. advertisements The new travel document incorporates modern security measures while reflecting Somalia’s national identity, cultural heritage and traditions. The meeting focused on implementing EAC Council of Ministers’ decisions, harmonising immigration procedures and improving cooperation between member states. Officials also discussed the recognition of national identity cards, the modernisation of immigration services and measures to facilitate the movement of people across the region. EAC passport integration The presentation follows Somalia’s approval to adopt and issue the EAC electronic passport, a key requirement in the country’s efforts to align its travel documents with regional standards. In February 2026, Somalia’s Ambassador to Tanzania and Permanent Representative to the EAC, Ilyas Ali Hassan, formally handed over the authorisation to Somali Internal Security Minister Abdullahi Sheikh Ismail, known as Fartaag. The authorisation, granted in December 2025, allowed Somalia to adopt the EAC passport’s approved design and proceed with preparations for its issuance. Somalia has since been working to modernise its travel documentation and strengthen immigration cooperation with other member states. The EAC electronic passport was first launched during the bloc’s 17th Ordinary Heads of State Summit on 2 March 2016. It is issued in three categories: ordinary, service and diplomatic passports, replacing older national passports in participating countries. The document is designed to strengthen travel security, improve border management and facilitate regional mobility. Somalia officially joined the East African Community on 4 March 2024, becoming the regional bloc’s eighth member state. Since joining, Mogadishu has been working to align its policies and institutions with regional commitments, particularly in immigration, trade and the movement of people. The introduction of the electronic passport represents another step towards meeting those obligations and strengthening Somalia’s participation in the regional bloc. According to the latest Henley Passport Index, Somalia ranks 99th globally, with its passport providing access to 32 destinations without a prior visa. somalia.content: Uganda sends new air force contingent to Somalia despite planned troop drawdown - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Uganda sends new air force contingent to Somalia despite planned troop drawdown Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Friday November 27, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — Uganda has deployed a new military aviation unit to Somalia under the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), reaffirming its commitment to the peacekeeping operation amid plans to gradually reduce its military presence in the country. In a statement issued Thursday, Nov. 26, the Uganda Peoples' Defence Forces (UPDF) said Aviation Unit VI was officially flagged off during a ceremony at Soroti Air Force Base in eastern Uganda. advertisements The unit will be commanded by Col. Simon Andiandu, with Maj. Ssempa Ndaula serving as deputy commander. The ceremony was presided over by Ugandan Air Force Commander Lt. Gen. Charles Okidi, who urged the deploying personnel to maintain discipline, professionalism and teamwork while carrying out their mission in Somalia. “This ceremony here today marks the formal deployment of Aviation Unit VI under UGABAG XLVIII. This is a testament to our continued effort and unwavering commitment to regional peace, security and stability on the African continent,” Okidi said. He told the troops that their deployment carried significant responsibilities and urged them to remain committed despite the challenges they could encounter during their mission. The Chief of Staff of the Ugandan Air Force, Brig. Gen. James Itungo, also addressed the personnel, describing them as representatives of Uganda and urging them to demonstrate professionalism and sound judgment throughout their deployment. Itungo called on the troops to remain alert to the operational environment and carry out their duties with confidence and discipline. Soroti Air Force Wing Commander Brig. Gen. Collin Mbaga Nkwasibwe said the personnel had undergone specialized training tailored to their operational responsibilities, including engineering and aviation security. The UPDF statement did not disclose the number of personnel being deployed, the aircraft assigned to the unit or the specific locations where they would operate in Somalia. The deployment comes just days after Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met in Entebbe on Nov. 23 and called for intensified military operations against al-Shabab. In a joint communiqué, the two leaders emphasized the need for predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM and alternative financing arrangements to support forces deployed under bilateral security agreements. Uganda has played a major role in African Union military operations in Somalia since 2007, contributing ground troops and other military capabilities to successive peacekeeping missions. However, Kampala has recently begun withdrawing troops deployed under bilateral arrangements with Somalia and has outlined plans for a gradual drawdown of its AUSSOM contingent by the end of 2027. The deployment of Aviation Unit VI comes amid those broader discussions about the future of Uganda's military presence and the transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. The UPDF did not indicate whether the aviation unit would replace an existing contingent or increase the number of Ugandan personnel serving under AUSSOM. AUSSOM, which succeeded the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) in January 2025, supports Somali security forces in operations against al-Shabab and the gradual transfer of security responsibilities to national institutions. Uganda remains one of the mission's key troop-contributing countries as Somali and African Union officials seek continued international support for counterterrorism operations and the security transition. somalia.title: African Union Endorses Three-Phase AUSSOM Exit, Warns Against Funding-Driven Drawdown - FTL Somalia
somalia.content: African Union Endorses Three-Phase AUSSOM Exit, Warns Against Funding-Driven Drawdown - Somali News today Live Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Security Nationwide African Union Endorses Three-Phase AUSSOM Exit, Warns Against Funding-Driven Drawdown November 27, 2026 5 min read ADDIS ABABA , The African Union’s Peace and Security Council endorsed a three-phase integrated transition plan for AUSSOM on November 25, approving a phased and sequenced reduction of the mission’s footprint that begins with the current period through December 2026 and extends through 2027, with a post-2027 arrangement to be determined. The communiqué, adopted at the Council’s 1380th meeting, follows the joint operational planning meeting held in Mogadishu from November 18 to 22, which brought together the African Union, the Federal Government of Somalia, AUSSOM troop and police contributing countries, and the United Nations. The plan outlines Phase One from November to December 2026, Phase Two from January to December 2027, and Phase Three covering the period after 2027. A Warning Against Uncoordinated Withdrawal The Council’s most pointed language was reserved for the risks of a hasty exit. It stressed that a “funding-driven, uncoordinated drawdown, as opposed to a deliberate and jointly sequenced transition, risks creating exploitable gaps that Al-Shabaab could use to retake strategic towns and main supply routes, reversing years of hard-won gains within a short period.” That warning reflects the reality that the mission’s future has been shaped as much by financial constraints as by strategic planning. The African Union has projected a need for approximately $190 million to facilitate the transition from its predecessor ATMIS, a shortfall FTL Somalia reported as the mission’s funding remained uncertain. The communiqué calls on the UN Security Council, the European Union, AU member states, and bilateral partners to provide financial and logistical support to AUSSOM, a request that has been repeated across multiple communiqués without corresponding commitments. The Council also requested that the AU Commission initiate diplomatic engagements to secure an extension of the UNSOS mandate through December 31, 2027, with adequate resources, to support the orderly reduction of AUSSOM’s footprint. UNSOS provides logistical support to the mission, and its mandate is separate from AUSSOM’s own authorization. Operational Gains and Political Paralysis The communiqué commends the Somali security forces for recent operations, including joint SSF-AUSSOM operations named “Silent Storm” and “Rolling Thunder,” and notes the transfer of authority over five locations to Somali forces. It also welcomes the holding of direct local elections in various regions and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s engagements with political parties and civil society. But the Council’s endorsement of the transition plan sits alongside a domestic political crisis that the communiqué does not directly address. The Chief Justice has ordered Parliament to suspend all legislative activities, declaring that its mandate expired in April 2026, a directive FTL Somalia reported . The Supreme Court has ruled that the President’s term ended in May 2026, and the government has rejected the ruling while continuing to function. The Cabinet approved electoral law amendments on November 24, changes FTL Somalia covered , but the Parliament that must pass them has been ordered to stop working. The communiqué’s emphasis on the “necessity for all Somali stakeholders to remain open for sustained engagements aimed at achieving a credible and broad-based consensus” is a diplomatic formulation that acknowledges the divisions without naming them. The Council is endorsing a security transition that depends on a political settlement the Somali government and its opponents have not reached. FTL Critical Note The Peace and Security Council’s communiqué is a carefully worded document that endorses a transition plan while warning against the conditions that could make it fail. The Council’s language on the risks of an uncoordinated drawdown is the most candid assessment of AUSSOM’s predicament to emerge from the African Union in months. It acknowledges, in diplomatic terms, that the mission’s exit could be driven by funding rather than strategy, and that the consequences could be catastrophic. But the communiqué also reflects the limits of what the African Union can do. The Council can endorse a plan, request support, and urge stakeholders to engage. It cannot generate the resources that the mission needs, and it cannot resolve the political crisis that has paralyzed the Somali institutions the transition is meant to empower. The request to extend UNSOS’s mandate is a recognition that the logistical architecture supporting AUSSOM must outlast the mission itself. But the United Nations Security Council has its own calculations, and its members have shown little appetite for open-ended commitments in Somalia. The three-phase plan is orderly on paper. Phase One, the current period, is already underway and faces a December 31 deadline for the mission’s authorization. Phase Two, covering 2027, depends on the Somali security forces’ ability to assume responsibility for transferred locations, and on the political will of a government whose own mandate is contested. Phase Three, post-2027, is described in the communiqué as a subject for “political and strategic discussion” rather than a defined arrangement. The plan’s most important phase is the one that has not yet been designed. The Council has bought time. Whether that time is used to build a sustainable security architecture or simply to postpone an unavoidable reckoning remains to be seen. Privacy Policy Terms of Service Search Museveni's Clout As Mediator Tested As Somalia Opposition Looks To Uganda Ahead Of 2027 Polls November 27, 2026 3 min read Listen By Asha Elmi - Editor-in-Chief MOGADISHU, 27 November 2026 — When Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni brokered the Kampala Accord in June 2011, his troops were the backbone of the African Union force in Somalia and guarded the country's top leaders. Fifteen years later, as some in Somalia's opposition look to him to break a political deadlock, analysts say his influence is far more limited. Museveni accepted an invitation to visit Somalia after talks with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in Entebbe on Nov. 23. The visit has raised hopes among some opposition figures that he could mediate in their dispute with the government over elections due next year. But the joint communique from the Entebbe meeting did not mention elections or any mediation role for Uganda. It focused on trade, security and counter-terrorism cooperation, and called for dialogue between the federal government and member states. WHAT HAPPENED IN 2011 Under the Kampala Accord, signed on June 9, 2011, President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and parliament speaker Sharif Hassan Sheikh Aden agreed to delay elections by a year. The prime minister, Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo, was required to resign within 30 days, and he did so on June 19. Museveni signed as a witness and was named as guarantor of the deal. At the time, Ugandan troops were the largest contingent in the African Union mission. Somalia had no strong national army, and the weak transitional government depended on AU forces for its survival. WHAT HAS CHANGED Uganda now has about 4,500 troops in the AU mission, AUSSOM, and about 2,000 more under a bilateral agreement with Somalia. The Ugandan army began withdrawing its bilateral troops in early November. Somalia has meanwhile built its own forces, including U.S.-trained Danab special forces and Turkish-trained Gorgor commandos. Related articles Emegha's Brace Not Enough as Hosts Nottingham Forest Beat Chelsea 3-2 AU Says Five Bases Handed to Somali Forces as Troop Reduction Begins "Ugandan troops were guarding the president, the prime minister and the speaker of parliament at their doors. Today none of that exists," Ali Nur Salad, director general of Dawan Media, said on the outlet's Politiko 360 podcast. He said Museveni's standing as an elder statesman could help, but that Uganda no longer had the leverage to force either side to the table. He also said Uganda had financial reasons to keep its troops in Somalia and was unlikely to withdraw them to pressure the government. WHY THE OPPOSITION LOOKS ABROAD Opposition leaders say they cannot rely on an agreement made with Hassan Sheikh alone, and want a foreign guarantor to ensure any deal is implemented. Efforts by Western partners and others to bring the two sides together have so far failed. Relations between Hassan Sheikh and neighbouring Ethiopia and Kenya, whose troops also serve in Somalia, have been strained. Hassan Sheikh has said Somali disputes should not be taken abroad. He has offered to meet opposition leaders at their homes, and former Prime Minister Abdi Farah Shirdoon has offered to host talks. Hussein Abdi Aden, Dawan Media's elections editor, said opposition leaders told the outlet they were not yet ready to discuss the Shirdoon initiative. He said Farmaajo, who lost his job under the 2011 deal, had welcomed Museveni's upcoming visit. The U.S. backed a one-year renewal of support for AUSSOM and the U.N. support office UNSOS on Nov. 15, which affects funding for Ugandan troops in Somalia. somalia.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni's role as a mediator in Somalia is being scrutinized as the opposition looks to him for assistance ahead of the 2027 elections. Museveni, who previously brokered the Kampala Accord in 2011, accepted an invitation to visit Somalia following discussions with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. However, the recent joint communique from their meeting focused on trade and security rather than electoral mediation, raising doubts about Museveni's current influence. Analysts suggest that while Museveni's status as an elder statesman could be beneficial, Uganda's leverage has diminished significantly since 2011, when its troops were crucial to Somalia's stability. The Somali opposition is wary of relying solely on agreements with the government and seeks a foreign guarantor for any potential deal. Despite strained relations with neighboring countries, Hassan Sheikh has proposed local discussions with opposition leaders, while the U.S. continues to support Ugandan troops in Somalia.

somalia.title: Türkiye inaugurates renovated school, breaks ground for hospital expansion in Somalia’s Middle Shabelle region - Hiiraan Online
somalia.content: Türkiye inaugurates renovated school, breaks ground for hospital expansion in Somalia’s Middle Shabelle region - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Türkiye inaugurates renovated school, breaks ground for hospital expansion in Somalia’s Middle Shabelle region Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Mohamed Dhaysane Friday November 27, 2026 Projects mark latest phase of Türkiye’s support for Somalia’s education and health care sectors, Turkish Embassy says Türkiye has inaugurated a renovated school and laid the foundation stone for a hospital expansion in Warsheikh, in Somalia’s Middle Shabelle region, the Turkish Embassy in Mogadishu said Thursday. The ceremony included the inauguration of a renovated primary and secondary school in Warsheikh and the launch of a major hospital rehabilitation and expansion project, marking the latest phase of Türkiye’s support for Somalia’s education and health care sectors, the embassy said in a statement. advertisements The Turkish Embassy said the projects were implemented in cooperation with Türkiye’s Defense Ministry, the Somali Turkish Task Force Command and Albayrak Group. “This aimed at expanding healthcare services for residents of the district and surrounding communities”, the Turkish embassy in Somalia said. The developments came days after Türkiye broke ground in Mogadishu for the new headquarters of the Somali Naval Forces, a Joint Operations Center and related facilities. The groundbreaking took place during a visit to Somalia by Turkish Chief of General Staff Gen. Selcuk Bayraktaroglu, who was hosted by Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud at the presidential palace in Mogadishu on Saturday. Türkiye is one of Somalia’s closest security partners, and bilateral ties have deepened since Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan visited Somalia in 2011, when he was prime minister. Türkiye’s military training mission in Somalia, known as TURKSOM, has supported the country’s counterterrorism operations by providing military training and logistical support to Somali security forces in their fight against terrorist groups such as al-Shabaab and Daesh. somalia.title: KSrelief Distributes 846 Food Baskets in Somalia - وكالة الأنباء السعودية
somalia.content: KSrelief Distributes 846 Food Baskets in Somalia
somalia.summary:
The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has distributed 846 food baskets in Somalia as part of its ongoing efforts to alleviate food insecurity in the region. This initiative aims to support vulnerable families affected by the ongoing humanitarian crisis. Each food basket contains essential items to meet the nutritional needs of families, ensuring they have access to basic sustenance. The distribution is part of a broader strategy by KSrelief to provide humanitarian assistance and improve living conditions for those in need. The organization continues to work in various regions of Somalia, addressing the challenges posed by drought, conflict, and economic instability. Through such initiatives, KSrelief aims to enhance food security and support the resilience of affected communities. The distribution reflects the commitment of KSrelief to provide timely and effective aid to those suffering from the impacts of humanitarian crises in Somalia.

football.title: مدرب الهلال أمام اختبار الثقة والتصحيح في دوري أبطال أفريقيا - winwin
football.content: مدرب الهلال أمام اختبار الثقة والتصحيح في دوري أبطال أفريقيا مدرب الهلال أمام اختبار الثقة والتصحيح في دوري أبطال أفريقيا مباريات اليوم رياضات كرة القدم الأخبار فيديو البطولات البرامج دول مدرب الهلال أمام اختبار الثقة والتصحيح في دوري أبطال أفريقيا جوزيف زينباور مدرب الهلال السوداني (Facebook/alhilalsc.official) 27 نوفمبر 2026 مدرب الهلال أمام اختبار الثقة والتصحيح في دوري أبطال أفريقيا الهلال السوداني دوري أبطال أفريقيا الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أضفنا الى 'غوغل' كثف الهلال السوداني تحضيراته لمواجهة ضيفه حوريا كوناكري الغيني، يوم الأحد 29 نوفمبر/ تشرين الثاني، على ملعب "أماهورو" بعاصمة رواندا كيغالي، ضمن الجولة الأولى من منافسات المجموعة الرابعة في دوري أبطال أفريقيا . ويطمح "الموج الأزرق" إلى انطلاقة قوية في مستهل مشواره بالمجموعات عبر تحقيق الفوز، مستفيدًا من خبرات نجومه وتواضع مستوى المنافس. وفي المقابل، يسعى المدرب جوزيف زينباور إلى استعادة ثقة الجماهير وتجاوز التراجع الفني الذي أثار مقارنات سلبية بين أداء الفريق في الموسم الماضي والحالي، ليجد نفسه أمام 3 تحديات صعبة. زينباور في اختبار تصحيح المسار تعرض زينباور لانتقادات لاذعة بسبب تذبذب مستوى الفريق، مما دفع الجماهير للمقارنة بين الحقبة الحالية للمدرب الألماني الذي يبلغ من العمر 56 عامًا، وما قدمه الفريق سابقًا تحت قيادة لورينتو ريجيكامب. وتعد مباريات دور المجموعات فرصة مثالية للمدرب الألماني لتصحيح المسار وإعادة الفريق إلى سكة الأداء المعهود. الهلال ومشكلة التشكيل المثالي استهلك المدرب الألماني وقتًا طويلًا دون أن يهتدي إلى التشكيل الأمثل، إذ واجه صعوبة بالغة في الاستقرار على عناصر ثابتة في مراكز الوسط والهجوم، ورغم خوضه 4 مباريات في الأدوار التمهيدية و7 في الدوري الرواندي، ظل التشكيل غير مستقر قبل أن يبدأ مؤخرًا في تثبيت عناصره استعدادًا للمواجهات المرتقبة في دور المجموعات. تحسين صورته وتخفيف حدة الانتقادات يسعى المدرب، الذي يقضي موسمه الأول مع الفريق، إلى تحسين صورته بعد الانتقادات الإعلامية والجماهيرية التي طالته إثر أنباء مفاوضاته مع ناديه السابق "الرجاء" ورغبته في الرحيل، مما أثار غضب المشجعين؛ لذا يطمح إلى تحقيق فوز مقنع في المباراة الافتتاحية أمام حوريا كوناكري ليمنح نفسه قدرًا من الأريحية ويستعيد ثقة الجماهير. اقرأ أيضا الهلال السوداني يستنفر ودعم جديد لزينباور قبل موعد حوريا الهلال يستهل حملة الدفاع عن لقبه بفوز ثمين بالدوري السوداني ويواجه بطل الدوري السوداني تحديات شاقة في النسخة الحالية من البطولة الأفريقية؛ إذ سيلاقي حوريا كوناكري الغيني يوم الأحد 29 نوفمبر على ملعب "أماهورو" في كيغالي ضمن الجولة الأولى، ثم يحل ضيفًا على المغرب الفاسي في 5 ديسمبر/ كانون الأول، قبل أن يستقبل بيراميدز المصري في 18 من الشهر نفسه ضمن قمة مباريات الجولة الثالثة. النشرة البريدية اشترك معنا بالنشرة البريدية لتصلك آخر أخبار الرياضة اشترك معنا دول كرة القدم الأخبار الدوريات الفرق رياضات التنس كرة السلة رياضات ميكانيكية مبارايات اليوم الأخبار البرامج الفيديو عن الموقع تواصل معنا أعلن معنا وظائف سياسة الخصوصية الشروط football.summary: يستعد فريق الهلال السوداني لمواجهة حوريا كوناكري الغيني في الجولة الأولى من دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا، والتي ستقام يوم الأحد 29 نوفمبر في ملعب "أماهورو" بالعاصمة الرواندية كيغالي. يسعى المدرب جوزيف زينباور، الذي يواجه انتقادات بسبب تراجع أداء الفريق، إلى استعادة ثقة الجماهير وتحقيق انطلاقة قوية في البطولة. بعد مقارنات سلبية مع أداء الفريق في الموسم الماضي، يأمل زينباور في تصحيح المسار وتحسين صورته بعد شائعات حول رغبته في مغادرة الفريق. يواجه المدرب تحديات في تحديد التشكيل المثالي، حيث لم يستقر على عناصر ثابتة في الوسط والهجوم رغم خوضه عدة مباريات. تحقيق فوز مقنع في المباراة الافتتاحية سيكون خطوة مهمة لتهدئة الانتقادات واستعادة ثقة المشجعين، حيث يواجه الهلال تحديات كبيرة في النسخة الحالية من البطولة الأفريقية.

football.summary: تستعد أندية الزمالك وبيراميدز لمنافسات الجولة الأولى من دور مجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا لموسم 2026-2027. حيث تأهل الزمالك بعد تخطيه الجيش الرواندي، وسيواجه الإفريقي التونسي يوم السبت المقبل على استاد القاهرة. من جهة أخرى، تأهل بيراميدز بعد الفوز على المريخ السوداني، ويستهل مشواره بمواجهة المغرب الفاسي في نفس اليوم. تتضمن مواعيد مباريات الجولة الأولى يوم السبت 28 نوفمبر 2026، لقاء يانج أفريكانز مع مولودية الجزائر في الساعة 3:00 مساءً، ومباراة بيراميدز ضد المغرب الفاسي في الساعة 6:00 مساءً، ومواجهة الزمالك مع الإفريقي التونسي في نفس التوقيت. كما ستقام مباريات أخرى مثل الترجي التونسي ضد ويليت الأنجولي ونهضة بركان المغربي ضد كولومب سبورتيف الكاميروني في أوقات مختلفة. يتطلع عشاق كرة القدم لمتابعة هذه المواجهات المثيرة.

(Facebook/Al Hilal S.C) 26 نوفمبر 2026 الهلال السوداني يستنفر ودعم جديد لزينباور قبل موعد حوريا الهلال السوداني هورويا دوري أبطال أفريقيا كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أعلنت إدارة نادي الهلال السوداني حالة الطوارئ استعدادًا لمواجهة ضيفه حوريا كوناكري الغيني، المقررة يوم الأحد 29 نوفمبر/ تشرين الثاني على ملعب "أماهورو" في العاصمة كيغالي، ضمن الجولة الأولى من منافسات المجموعة الرابعة لمسابقة دوري أبطال أفريقيا . ودعت إدارة "النادي الأزرق" جماهيرها لمؤازرة الفريق، وقررت فتح أبواب الملعب مجانًا لضمان حضور جماهيري حاشد يدعم اللاعبين في مستهل مشوارهم بدور المجموعات، في ظل التحديات الصعبة التي تنتظر الفريق أمام كل من حوريا كوناكري، والمغرب الفاسي، وبيراميدز المصري. الهلال السوداني يترقب مساندة جماهيرية ضخمة أسهمت المشاركة المشتركة للهلال ومواطنه المريخ بالدوري الرواندي في تحقيق دعم جماهيري لافت، أدى لاختيار ملعب "أماهورو" لاستضافة مباريات الفريق، وهو ما منحه دفعة معنوية كبيرة في النسخة الحالية والسابقة من البطولة الأفريقية. اقرأ أيضًا الهلال يستهل حملة الدفاع عن لقبه بفوز ثمين بالدوري السوداني بريمونتادا مثيرة.. الهلال يخطف صدارة الدوري الرواندي ومع تقدم الهلال في المنافسة، حرصت إدارة النادي على تعزيز هذا الحضور بتوفير تذاكر مجانية ووسائل نقل للجماهير. ومن المتوقع أن تشهد مباراة الفريق مع حوريا كوناكري حضورًا جماهيريًا غفيرًا، خاصة في ظل تطلعات الفريق لتحقيق الفوز وحصد النقاط الثلاث الأولى، مما يعزز حظوظه في بلوغ ربع النهائي للمرة الثالثة على التوالي. زينباور يتلقى المزيد من الدعم وعزز المدرب جوزيف زينباور جاهزية فريقه بخوض مباراتين قويتين في الدوري الرواندي عقب فترة التوقف الدولي. وتلقى المدرب الألماني دفعة معنوية بعودة نجمه أداما كوليبالي، الذي استعاد عافيته بعد غياب طويل بسبب الإصابة وأنهى برنامجه التأهيلي ليصبح جاهزا لدعم الخط الهجومي بمشاركته في المباريات مؤخرًا، ما يمنحه جاهزية ستدعم المقدمة الهجومية لا سيما في ظل التراجع الفني الواضح بالموسم الحالي. وفي السياق ذاته، بدأ مدرب الفريق السوداني بإشراك النجم حاج ماديكي تدريجيا لتهيئته للمباريات المقبلة؛ علما بأن كوليبالي وماديكي يعدان من العناصر المؤثرة التي بصمت على أداء لافت في النسخة الماضية من البطولة. ويطمح رفاق القائد محمد عبد الرحمن إلى مواصلة تألقهم في الأدوار المتقدمة من البطولة الأفريقية، إذ وضعت إدارة النادي بلوغ نصف النهائي هدفًا مبدئيًا بالنسخة الحالية من البطولة، مع استهداف التتويج باللقب القاري بحلول عام 2028، وذلك في إطار مساعي النادي لتجاوز تداعيات الحرب التي اندلعت في البلاد منتصف أبريل 2023. أخبار ذات صلة المريخ قبل الديربي.. المريخ يسعى لتحقيق هدف خاص في رواندا! 27 football.summary: تستعد مباراة الأهلي مروي ضد السهم الرياضي الدامر في الدوري السوداني الممتاز، والتي ستقام في 30 نوفمبر 2026، في استاد كريمة. المباراة تأتي ضمن الجولة الثانية من مرحلة الدوري، حيث يتنافس الفريقان في المجموعة A. الأهلي مروي يسعى لتحقيق الفوز لتعزيز موقفه في الدوري، بينما السهم الرياضي الدامر يأمل في تقديم أداء قوي. حتى الآن، يتصدر المريخ المجموعة بعد فوزه في مباراته الأولى، يليه هلال الفاشر. يتضمن جدول الدوري الحالي فرقًا مثل أهلي الخرطوم وحي الوادي والفجر الأبيض، وكلها تتنافس على النقاط. المباراة ستكون متاحة للبث المباشر عبر منصة Winwin، مما يتيح للجماهير متابعة الأحداث لحظة بلحظة. هذه المباراة تمثل فرصة هامة لكل فريق لتعزيز رصيده من النقاط في بداية الموسم.

football.summary: في مباراة مثيرة ضمن الدوري السوداني الممتاز، حقق فريق الأهلي مروي فوزًا مهمًا على الهلال السوداني بنتيجة 1-0. أقيمت المباراة في استاد كريمة يوم 25 نوفمبر 2026، حيث سجل الأهلي مروي هدفه الوحيد في الشوط الأول. هذا الفوز يضع الأهلي مروي في بداية قوية للموسم، بينما يسعى الهلال للدفاع عن لقبه بعد أن بدأ الموسم بخسارة غير متوقعة. في جدول الدوري، يتصدر المريخ المجموعة بعد فوزه في مباراته الأولى، بينما يحتل الأهلي مروي المركز الثاني. المباراة كانت جزءًا من الجولة الأولى من الدوري، الذي شهد افتتاحًا استثنائيًا بمشاركة ثماني فرق. يتطلع الهلال إلى تحسين أدائه في المباريات القادمة بعد تعيين مدرب جديد، بينما يستمر الأهلي مروي في تقديم أداء قوي.
